q1_issues.issue: 'claimed TO treat, prevent, diagnose or cure' is a to-infinitive control complement, which the instruction set says never seals (sealing is finite-clause-only); the disjunction is sealed as a Theme term instead of reified beside the attitude with the controller's role copied in.
(Member sk_disease_1 specific) predicates a descriptive modifier of the group symbol; on a plural a descriptive modifier must distribute over the members, never sit on the group as an object.
'that kind of statement' is reduced to the bare class symbol 'statement', dropping the kind-anaphoric demonstrative that ties the prohibited statement type to the claims just described.

q2_gaps: kind-anaphoric 'that kind of N' / 'this sort of N' — no way to record the anaphoric link back to a previously described kind

equative/appositive 'or' ('55 percent, or 149') — the disjunction section directs every 'or' to an inclusive (Or …) unless an exclusivity cue fires, which would wrongly disjoin two descriptions of the same quantity

disjunction over the VERB of an otherwise shared clause ('treat, prevent, diagnose or cure X'): the narrowest-scope rule has no form that varies the event class while sharing one event witness, and wide scope is reserved for clauses that share nothing
plural demonstrative 'those' with an antecedent outside the passage — the anonymous-witness defaults cover he/she/it/they, so the member kind (person vs thing) is unspecified
notes: The partitive shape (definite superset, SubsetOf, Cardinality 149 beside the un-reduced (Fraction 55 100)), the per-verb role split (treat/prevent/cure Patient, diagnose Theme), the reduced relative 'the regulations prohibiting …', and the postposed concessive (Despite <main> <sub>) all follow the instruction set. Classing the unresolvable 'those' as a group of person is a world-knowledge stretch — the referents are the label claims, not people — but the pronoun defaults as written permit it.
